title: Civil Defence and Other Matters Bill
what_it_is: Civil Defence and Other Matters Bill

sections.label: Civil Defence Act amendment objectives
sections.summary: The Bill amends the Civil Defence Act to enhance SCDF operational response, codify officers' powers and protection, and strengthen disciplinary and HR processes.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: The Civil Defence Act (CD Act), provides for the establishment, maintenance and discipline of the Singapore Civil Defence Force (SCDF).

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: This Bill seeks to amend the CD Act to achieve three objectives: first, to enhance SCDF's operational response and efficiency; second, to codify the powers and protection that SCDF officers need to do their work effectively; third, to strengthen SCDF's disciplinary and human resource (HR) processes.

sections.label: Building owners non-compliance offence
sections.summary: New section 103B makes it an offence for building owners to not comply with a Commissioner's direction to provide space and access for civil defence emergency devices.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: New section 103B inserted by clause 20 of the Bill will, therefore, make it an offence for building owners to not comply with a direction from the Commissioner of SCDF to provide SCDF with space and access to the premises, for the installation of prescribed civil defence emergency devices, such as PWS sirens.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Non-compliant building owners will be liable for a fine of up to $10,000 and an imprisonment term of up to three years, as well as a further fine of up to $1,000 for each day of non-compliance after conviction.

sections.label: SCDF EMS patients in 2017
sections.summary: In 2017, SCDF attended to some 165,000 EMS patients.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: In 2017, SCDF attended to some 165,000 EMS patients.

sections.label: Fingerprints and identity disclosure powers
sections.summary: New section 101A(2) empowers officers to obtain identifiers of unknown, unconscious EMS patients, and clause 25 allows the Minister to authorise disclosure of identifying information.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: New section 101A(2) inserted by clause 18, therefore, proposes to empower SCDF officers and other authorised individuals attending to EMS calls to obtain the fingerprints or other personal identifiers of a patient whose identity is not known, and is unconscious or otherwise unable to communicate, for example, individuals who are having a seizure.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Clause 25 amends section 36B(2) of the Immigration Act to allow the Minister for Home Affairs to authorise the disclosure of identifying information belonging to an EMS patient, for the purpose of providing him with urgent medical care.

sections.label: Powers placed on legislative footing
sections.summary: Clause 18 places the requisite powers for these operations on an explicit legislative footing in the CD Act.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Clause 18 places on an explicit legislative footing the requisite powers for these operations in the CD Act.

sections.label: Legal protection for SCDF officers
sections.summary: New section 101C provides SCDF officers legal protection for actions undertaken in execution of the CD Act, including during civil defence operations.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: New section 101C inserted by clause 18, therefore, provides SCDF officers with legal protection for actions undertaken in execution of the CD Act, including during any civil defence operation.

sections.label: Powers for PAO crew, SAF medics
sections.summary: New section 101B extends EMS powers and legal liability protection to PAO crew members and SAF medics attending EMS calls.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: PAO crew members and SAF medics attending to EMS calls perform the same role as their SCDF counterparts and should be given the same powers and legal protection to do their jobs well.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Hence, the new section 101B inserted by clause 18 extends the requisite powers for EMS operations and protection from legal liability to PAO crew members and SAF medics, when they are attending to EMS calls.

sections.label: SCDF NSmen service beyond maximum age
sections.summary: New section 9A lets SCDF NSmen serve beyond the maximum service age if willing and required by SCDF.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: The new section 9A inserted by clause 7 allows SCDF NSmen to serve beyond the stipulated maximum service age, if they are willing to do so and their services are required by SCDF.

sections.label: Offence for refusing medical order
sections.summary: New section 32A makes it a service offence for an SCDF officer not to comply with a Commissioner's order for medical examination or treatment.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: The new section 32A inserted by clause 12 makes it a service offence under the CD Act for an SCDF officer not to comply with an order from the Commissioner of SCDF to go for a medical examination or treatment.

sections.label: Trial period for SCDF NSmen
sections.summary: Clause 11 amends section 19(1) so SCDF NSmen may be tried within three years from when the offence was reported or discovered.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: To address situations where offences may only come to light later, clause 11 amends section 19(1) to provide for SCDF NSmen to be tried within three years, from the day the offence was reported or discovered.

sections.label: Compelling NSmen to report for trial
sections.summary: Clause 10 amends section 18 to let SCDF issue orders compelling NSmen who committed service offences to report for summary trial.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Clause 10 amends section 18 to allow SCDF to issue orders under the CD Act to compel NSmen who have committed service offences to report for summary trial.

sections.label: Appeals against summary trial outcomes
sections.summary: Clause 15 inserts new section 76A providing a mechanism for SCDF NSmen to appeal findings or punishment awards.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: To strengthen the summary trial process, clause 15 inserts a new section 76A which provides a new mechanism for SCDF NSmen to appeal against the findings or award of punishments.

sections.label: Penalty fine and imprisonment
sections.summary: The penalty is a fine of up to $2,500 and imprisonment of up to six months.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: The penalty will be a fine of up to $2,500 and an imprisonment term of up to six months.

sections.label: SCDF NSmen voluntary service extension
sections.summary: The Bill strengthens HR capacity by allowing SCDF NSmen to voluntarily extend service beyond what is required.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: The first main feature of this Bill is that it strengthens HR capacity by allowing SCDF NSmen to voluntarily extend their service beyond what is required.

sections.label: SCDF functions beyond firefighting
sections.summary: The Bill expands the SCDF's functions beyond firefighting to provide statutory powers for day-to-day life-saving duties not involving fighting fires.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: The Bill expands the scope of the SCDF's functions to go beyond firefighting so as to provide statutory-based powers needed for their day-to-day life-saving duties which do not involve fighting fires.

sections.label: Clause 20 emergency devices access
sections.summary: Clause 20 involves access to install and maintain emergency devices that act as public warning devices or monitor or detect a civil defence emergency.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: The first is clause 20 which involves access to install and maintain emergency devices which act as a public warning device or to monitor or detect a civil defence emergency.

sections.label: Biometric identification of unconscious persons
sections.summary: A further power is the ability to take biometric identification factors to identify an unconscious person or one unable to communicate for medical intervention.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: A further additional power is the ability to take biometric identification factors to identify an unconscious person or one who is unable to communicate for medical intervention.

sections.label: 2016 public perception survey confidence
sections.summary: The 2016 public perception survey showed overall public confidence in SCDF coping with emergencies reached a high of 99%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: The public perception survey of 2016 showed that “the overall public confidence with SCDF being capable to cope with emergencies reached a high at 99%”.

sections.label: MHA Press Release non-fire emergencies
sections.summary: The MHA Press Release states non-fire emergencies could include responding to emergency medical services calls.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: First, the official Press Release by MHA states that such non-fire emergencies could include responding to emergency medical services calls.

sections.label: Clause 7 ex-NS SCDF volunteers
sections.summary: Clause 7 introduces a scheme letting ex-NS men enlisted in SCDF continue serving as volunteers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Second, clause 7 introduces a new scheme allowing ex-NS men who were enlisted in SCDF to continue serving as volunteers.

sections.label: Building owners outdoor siren access
sections.summary: The Bill requires building owners to provide space and grant SCDF officers access to install, maintain and repair outdoor sirens and other emergency devices.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Third, I understand that the Bill also requires building owners to provide space and grant SCDF officers access to install, maintain and repair the outdoor sirens that are part of PWS as well as other emergency devices.

sections.label: Fingerprints of unconscious patients
sections.summary: The Bill allows SCDF officers attending medical emergencies to collect fingerprints and personal identifiers of unconscious patients.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Under the Bill, SCDF officers attending to medical emergencies will be allowed to collect the fingerprints and other personal identifiers of unconscious patients.

sections.label: Criminalising unauthorised SCDF uniforms insignia
sections.summary: The Bill proposes to criminalise unauthorised production, sale, distribution and use of SCDF uniforms and insignia to deter impersonators.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Due to the protection conferred upon SCDF officers, the Bill proposes to criminalise any unauthorised production, sale, distribution and use of SCDF uniforms and insignia, to deter abuse by impersonators.

sections.label: Peacetime powers and liability protection
sections.summary: The Bill gives SCDF officers explicit peacetime powers, requiring good faith and reasonable care, and extends protection from personal liability to peacetime situations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: The Bill makes changes to the CD Act to give explicit powers to SCDF officers for peacetime civil defence operations and, as stated by the hon Minister, to enhance the SCDF's operational response and effectiveness.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: In connection with this, the Bill proposes that the powers given to SCDF officers must be exercised in good faith and with reasonable care, and, if so, the SCDF officers will not be personally liable for any act or omission carried out in the execution of such powers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: This protection from personal liability presently applies in civil defence emergency situations but will now be extended to peacetime situations.

sections.label: AED cabinet educational sticker
sections.summary: A new educational sticker with step-by-step instructions on handling suspected cardiac arrest will be affixed to every AED cabinet in HDB blocks by July 2019.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: The hon Minister, in his answer, informed that a new educational sticker, with clear step-by-step instructions on how to handle suspected cardiac arrest cases, will be affixed to the bottom left of every AED cabinet installed in HDB blocks by July 2019.

sections.label: SCDF officers legal liability protection
sections.summary: The amendment is broad, and the speaker is concerned about the caveat requiring officers to act in good faith and with reasonable care.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: The amendment is so wide that it is as general as section 115(1) which already states that the Minister may make regulations for carrying out or giving effect to the provisions of this Act.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: The explicit legal powers currently granted to our SCDF officers are limited to firefighting operations, Civil Defence operations during a state of emergency or state of Civil Defence emergency.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: However, our officers also assist in rescues involving EMSes and other life-and-death situations, such as worksite and traffic accidents.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Hence, it is only right that they are protected from legal liability when they are part of such hazardous operations.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: I am concerned about the caveat that requires officers to "act in good faith and with reasonable care" in the course of their duties.

sections.label: Protection for officers if sued
sections.summary: The passage asks what measures are available to protect officers if something goes wrong and victims' family members pursue further action.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: What measures are available to protect these officers if something goes wrong and family members of victims decide to pursue further action?

sections.label: Hazardous materials detection devices study
sections.summary: SCDF is studying the feasibility of installing devices that can detect hazardous materials in the air, such as chemicals or radiological substances.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: SCDF is studying the feasibility of installing devices that can detect hazardous materials in the air, such as chemicals or radiological substances.

sections.label: Ambulance fingerprint scanning device
sections.summary: SCDF will equip ambulance crews with a mobile device that scans a patient's fingerprint and checks it remotely against ICA's database to obtain information from NEHR.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: SCDF will equip the ambulance crew with a mobile device that can scan the patient's fingerprint and check it remotely against ICA's database.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: If there is a match, the patient's national registration identity card or foreign identification number (FIN) number will be provided to obtain the relevant information from the National Electronic Health Record (NEHR) system.

sections.label: Data security measures for devices
sections.summary: Examples include measures against hacking, encryption, password protection, auto-lockdown, auto-wipe of data, and regular purging of data from devices.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Examples include measures against hacking, encryption of information, password protection, measures against multiple unsuccessful log-ins, such as the auto-lockdown of the account and the auto-wipe of data stored on the device, and regular purging of data from the devices.

sections.label: Impersonating Home Team officers
sections.summary: Melvin Yong asked about ill-intentioned individuals impersonating Home Team officers, and the answer is yes, with examples of SCDF and ICA impersonation.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Mr Melvin Yong asked whether there were cases where ill-intentioned individuals had impersonated Home Team officers, and the answer is yes.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Dressed in uniform and identifying themselves as SCDF officers, they had demanded to see the fire certificates of several shops at Jalan Bukit Merah and tried to sell fire extinguishers to the shop owners.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: In 2016, a man wore a uniform and posed as an ICA officer to steal contraband cigarettes.

sections.label: AEDs in HDB blocks
sections.summary: Under this initiative, SCDF is installing AEDs in HDB blocks island-wide.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Under this initiative, SCDF is installing AEDs in HDB blocks island-wide.

sections.label: Central fire alarm systems question
sections.summary: Louis Ng asked whether MHA will consider mandating central fire alarm systems in HDB blocks, and SCDF assesses Fire Code requirements are sufficient.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Mr Louis Ng asked whether MHA will consider mandating central fire alarm systems in HDB blocks.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Both do not require a central fire alarm system.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: SCDF’s assessment is that the Fire Code requirements for residential buildings are sufficient vis-à-vis the fire risks.

sections.label: No central fire alarm need
sections.summary: SCDF assesses there is no need to require central fire alarm systems in residential buildings.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Consequently, SCDF assesses that there is no need to require the installation of central fire alarm systems in residential buildings.
